title: Biryani, Sweets and Saplings: Tamil Nadu Celebrates CM Vijay's Final Film
excerpt: TVK ministers and fan clubs turned the release of Jana Nayagan into a statewide food festival, with biryani feasts, milk abhishekam and sapling drives marking the actor-turned-CM's swan song.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Tamil Nadu celebrated CM Vijay's film release with statewide biryani feasts and sapling distributions.
  • The film 'Jana Nayagan' grossed over ₹20 crore within hours of its release.
  • Pre-sales exceeded 1 million tickets across nearly 8,000 screens in 30 countries.
  • TVK instructed party members to decorate theatres and celebrate the film as a grand festival.
  • Community activities included milk abhishekam and cultural performances across multiple cities.
A Grand Festival for a Film Release
›Biryani served across Tamil Nadu.
›Sweets and saplings distributed by ministers.
›Traditional milk abhishekam performed by fans.
›Theatres decorated with party colors and banners.

Tamil Nadu's theatres doubled as community kitchens on July 23 as ministers, party workers and fan clubs marked the release of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's final film Jana Nayagan with biryani feasts, sweet distribution and sapling drives across the state. The food-driven celebrations, a longstanding tradition in South Indian cinema, reached an unprecedented scale as the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) mobilized its cadres for what the party called a "grand festival."

In Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu ministers served biryani to fans gathered outside theatres and distributed saplings as part of the festivities, according to ANI. In Coimbatore, Prohibition Minister K Vignesh led TVK functionaries and sanitation workers in a community clean-up drive in the Kinathukadavu area before heading to screenings.

"We are continuing the tradition."

— K Vignesh, Tamil Nadu Prohibition Minister, on organizing community activities for Vijay's film release

Feasts and Rituals Across the State

The biryani distribution in Kanchipuram was one piece of a statewide celebration that blended food, film and politics. In Thanjavur, fans performed traditional milk abhishekam — the pouring of milk over giant cutouts of the star — and danced to drum beats outside cinemas, according to News Arena India. In Chennai, fans at the iconic Rohini Silver Screens arrived before dawn for first-day-first-show screenings, many wearing TVK scarves and T-shirts.

Across Chennai, Madurai, Tiruchirappalli, Salem and Tirunelveli, TVK functionaries organized drum performances, fireworks, cultural programmes and the distribution of sweets, according to Chennai Vision. Many theatres were decorated with banners, flowers and party flags. Police were deployed outside major cinema complexes to manage the crowds.

TVK general secretary N Anand issued specific instructions to party workers, ministers, MLAs and district secretaries to celebrate the release as a "grand festival," directing them to decorate theatres screening the film in line with party guidelines, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

A ₹300-Crore Farewell on 8,000 Screens

Jana Nayagan, directed by H. Vinoth and produced by KVN Productions, is widely seen as Vijay's farewell to cinema after three decades in Tamil film. The actor became Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister in May 2026 through his TVK party, and the film's title card was modified to describe him as "the Honourable Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu."

The film opened to record-breaking numbers. Pre-sales crossed 1 million tickets in India, with BookMyShow recording 11.82 lakh tickets — placing it among the top five Tamil pre-sellers alongside Leo and Jailer, according to Sacnilk. By 3:15 PM on opening day, the film had collected ₹17 crore net across 7,176 tracked shows, with India gross surpassing ₹20 crore.

Capped Ticket Price in Chennai

Made on a budget of ₹300–500 crore, Jana Nayagan released across nearly 8,000 screens in 30 countries. In Tamil Nadu alone, the film was screened across roughly 1,000 theatres with over 3,500 shows. The state government capped ticket prices at ₹190 in Chennai to manage demand.

"An emotion for people across the globe."

— Venkat K Narayana, Producer, KVN Productions, on CM Vijay's significance

When Film Releases Become Community Feasts

The biryani and sweets distribution at Jana Nayagan screenings reflects a deeply rooted South Indian tradition where major film releases double as community celebrations. Fan clubs routinely organize mass feeding drives, marking the occasion with biryani — the undisputed celebration dish across Tamil Nadu, whether the event is a wedding, a political rally or a superstar's new release.

For the Tamil diaspora, these scenes resonate powerfully. The film's international advance bookings crossed $2 million (approximately ₹19.3 crore), and celebrations in overseas markets are expected to mirror the festive energy at home. Jana Nayagan is also releasing in Hindi as Janeta, in Telugu as Janayaku and in Kannada as Janayak.

Cultural Significance of Film Releases
›Biryani is a celebration staple in Tamil Nadu.
›Community feasts mark major film releases.
›Celebrations resonate with the Tamil diaspora.
›International advance bookings crossed $2 million.

With the evening shows still ahead on Day 1, industry watchers are tracking whether Jana Nayagan can enter the ₹1,000 crore club — a milestone that would be fuelled as much by the frenzy in theatres as by the biryani served outside them.
